glosses: To exhaust (someone); to tire (them) out.

examples.text: An hour of snow shoveling kind of wiped me out more than I expected.
I tried to force myself to sound happy even though I was exhausted. Four solid days of finals and studying for them had wiped me out.

glosses: To bankrupt (a person or company); to empty (a bank account); to erase (a bank balance).

examples.text: They tried hard to hang on, but the Great Depression wiped them out.
Unexpected big-ticket expenses wiped out his bank balance.

glosses: To crash; to fall over or fall off (especially in board sports such as surfing, skateboarding, etc.).

examples.text: shot into the half-pipe but then wiped out
A massive wave caused him to wipe out.

glosses: To knock (a surfer) off their board.

examples.text: A massive wave wiped him out.
I'd like to show you what a wipeout looks like from the board. I'm pretty good at getting wiped out, so I'll be the stooge.

glosses: Nonstandard form of wipeout; nonstandard but widespread.

translations.source_sense_description: исключать, устранять откуда-либо

glosses: To erase (as anything impressed or inscribed upon a surface); to render illegible or indiscernible.

examples.text: Do not efface what I've written on the chalkboard.
An outline of the same device might be traced on his shield, though many a blow had almost effaced the painting.

glosses: To cause to disappear as if by rubbing out or striking out.

examples.text: Some people like to efface their own memories with alcohol.
The bright records of the last hour effaced all the darker traces left by long and weary days.

glosses: To make oneself inobtrusive as if due to modesty or diffidence.

examples.text: Many people seem shy, but they really just efface for meekness.

glosses: Of the cervix during pregnancy, to thin and stretch in preparation for labor.
Of a woman: to have the cervix thin and stretch in this manner.

examples.text: Some females efface 75% by the 39th week of pregnancy.

translations.source_sense_description: исключать, устранять откуда-либо

glosses: To reduce to nothing, to destroy, to eradicate.

examples.text: An atom bomb can annihilate a whole city.

But eagerness in this case, as in most others, annihilated its own delight; down came the tottering height, while the disappointed builder found relief for his sorrow in anger—sorrow's best remedy after all.

glosses: To react with antimatter, producing gamma radiation and (for higher-mass reactants, especially composite particles such as protons) lighter particles (such as pions, muons, and neutrinos).
To treat as worthless, to vilify.

examples.text: of all the opinions which Antiquity hath had of men in gross, those which I most willingly embrace, and whereon I take most hold, are such as most vilifie, condemne, and annihilate us.

glosses: To render null and void; to abrogate.

translations.source_sense_description: исключать, устранять откуда-либо

glosses: To formally revoke the validity of.

examples.text: If you ask how religion thus falls on the thorns and faces death, and in the very act annuls annihilation, I cannot explain the matter, for it is religion's secret, and to understand it you must yourself have been a religious man of the extremer type.

glosses: To dissolve (a marital union) on the grounds that it is not valid.
